Ahmed, who has been stripped of his British citizenship, currently resides in the UK due to legal barriers that prevent his deportation. The Home Office has indicated it is exploring all options, including potential emergency legislation, to facilitate his removal to Pakistan.

A Home Office minister stated that the government remains "determined" to see Ahmed deported, highlighting ongoing discussions about the legal framework surrounding his case. Existing laws complicate the removal of certain Commonwealth citizens like Ahmed, dating back 50 years.

The case has drawn significant attention due to the serious nature of Ahmed's crimes and the implications of his continued presence in the UK.

articles.title: Boy, 3, dies after Middleton nursery incident as police open investigation
articles.excerpt: GMP says the boy died on 5 November after emergency services were called to Cosy Toes Nursery on 2 November. No arrests have been made.
articles.content_html:
A three-year-old boy has died after an emergency at a Middleton nursery, and police have opened an investigation into the circumstances.

Greater Manchester Police said on Wednesday 18 November that the boy died in hospital on Thursday 5 November. Emergency services had been called to Cosy Toes Nursery on Mainway East shortly before 4pm on Monday 2 November following a report of concern for a child.

Officers attended alongside other emergency services and the boy was taken to hospital. His family is being supported by specialist officers.

GMP said an investigation had been opened in line with usual procedure because the circumstances leading up to his death occurred in a care setting. No arrests have been made.

Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan said: "This is an incredibly tragic development in a deeply upsetting incident and our thoughts remain with the boy's family."

She added: "We are in the very early stages of our involvement and are carefully considering events and the evidence available to us. For now, we ask that the family's privacy is respected as they begin to navigate the unimaginable loss of their little boy."

The police statement gives no cause of death and makes no allegation of wrongdoing against any named person or organisation.

Anyone with information that could help the investigation can report it online to Greater Manchester Police or call 0161 856 3635. Information can also be given anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or through its website.

Update, 18 November 2026: This article previously reported that the boy was in a critical condition. It has been updated following GMP's confirmation of his death and the opening of an investigation.

articles.title: Rochdale Metrolink patrols target knife crime during Sceptre week
articles.excerpt: Town centre PCSOs have patrolled the tram route between Newbold and Rochdale town centre as part of the national knife crime campaign.
articles.content_html:
Police community support officers have carried out patrols on the Metrolink between Newbold and Rochdale town centre as part of a national campaign against knife crime.

PCSO Tyler Davies, from Rochdale Town Centre’s neighbourhood team, confirmed the activity in a police community alert published on Tuesday 17 November. The patrols form part of Operation Sceptre, which combines enforcement, prevention and community engagement.

The local alert reports the patrols but gives no figures for arrests or weapons recovered.

In a separate statement issued on Wednesday 18 November, Greater Manchester Police outlined plans for the national week of action. Across the force, these include weapons searches, visible patrols, targeted enforcement, test purchases in shops and sessions with schools and communities.

GMP said its school engagement officers work with schools across Greater Manchester on knife crime prevention, including support for teachers through the Pol-Ed education platform.

Detective Superintendent Richard Thompson, who leads the force’s response to knife crime and serious violence, said: "Whilst the progress we have seen in reducing knife-enabled robberies is positive, we are not complacent."

He said the campaign combines action against people carrying and using weapons with education and prevention. The force’s work continues throughout the year.

GMP also held an online question and answer session on Monday 16 November, covering topics including safe knife disposal and support for young people. The questions and answers remain available at https://app.sli.do/event/mPTtysYyVsSfUCZKNaxEmE/live/questions.

articles.excerpt: A three-year-old boy has died after an incident at Cosy Toes Nursery in Middleton, prompting a police investigation and the nursery's closure.
articles.content_html:
A three-year-old boy has died following an incident at Cosy Toes Nursery in Middleton on 2 November. Emergency services were called to the nursery shortly before 16:00 GMT, and the boy was taken to hospital, where he died three days later.

In response to the incident, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) have launched an investigation, which is standard procedure following a child's death in a care setting. No arrests have been made at this stage, and the boy's family is being supported by specialist officers.

Representatives from Cosy Toes Nursery expressed their heartbreak over the boy's death, describing him as a 'wonderful and beautiful child'. The nursery has been closed for six weeks following the incident, with its registration suspended by Ofsted while investigations are ongoing.

An Ofsted spokesperson stated, "Our thoughts are with the family of the young boy and everyone affected by this deeply distressing incident."

Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan from GMP described the situation as 'incredibly tragic' and urged respect for the family's privacy during this difficult time. Elsie Blundell, MP for Heywood & Middleton North, also expressed her condolences and highlighted the importance of the ongoing police investigation.

articles.title: World armwrestling champion Agi Gorzyńska to take on challengers at Rochdale's Grushka House
articles.excerpt: The three-time world champion will lead four free taster sessions on Drake Street on Sunday 6 December, with booking required for everyone.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale residents can test their strength against three-time world armwrestling champion Agi "Armpower" Gorzyńska at Grushka House on Drake Street on Sunday 6 December.

The free event runs from 11am to 5pm at the Polish community space, which recently opened in Rochdale town centre.

Ms Gorzyńska, a Polish athlete who represents Great Britain, has won three world titles and three European titles. The event poster also lists her as an eight-time British champion.

She will lead four sessions during the day, each lasting about 30 to 40 minutes. She will demonstrate armwrestling techniques, coach beginners and invite guests to try the sport under her guidance.

Visitors will also be able to meet her and have their photograph taken, with time for informal conversation between sessions.

Places are limited and advance booking is required for everyone, including spectators. Reservations are made by messaging Grushka House and are confirmed individually, and registration details are due to be posted on the venue's Facebook event page.

The event will include information about Zinzino products, as Ms Gorzyńska attends as a brand ambassador for the company. Food and drinks will be available to buy.

Grushka House was opened by Grazyna, who is known to her British friends as Grace. She described it as "a welcoming community space" serving coffee, cake and zapiekanka, a Polish toasted baguette with melted cheese and toppings.

The venue also hosts evening workshops, community events and social gatherings.

Before her Rochdale visit, Ms Gorzyńska is due to compete at the PAA Nationals on 28 and 29 November.

Grushka House is at 55 Drake Street, Rochdale, OL16 1RX.

articles.excerpt: A significant explosion occurred in Rochdale on 17 November, scattering debris across Bury Road and prompting a swift emergency response.
articles.content_html:
A massive explosion occurred in Rochdale on 17 November, scattering debris across Bury Road and prompting a significant emergency response.

The explosion was reported at an address on Camberley Drive shortly before rush hour. Residents in Milnrow reported hearing a loud bang and felt their cars shake due to the force of the explosion.

No injuries have been reported, and the cause of the explosion has not yet been confirmed, although earlier reports suggested a hot tub may have been involved.

Emergency services responded quickly, with firefighters working alongside other agencies to secure the area. Bury Road remains closed as investigations continue into the incident, which has left residents feeling fearful and confused.

The explosion has drawn attention from local authorities, and further updates are expected as investigations progress. Residents are advised to stay clear of the area while emergency services carry out their work.

articles.title: Rochdale man denies machete possession and window damage charges in Bury
articles.excerpt: Mayson Oldham, 21, of Balderstone Road, Rochdale, pleaded not guilty to charges of possessing a machete and damaging windows in Bury.
articles.content_html:
Mayson Oldham, 21, of Balderstone Road, Rochdale, has denied charges of possessing a machete and damaging windows in Bury.

He entered not guilty pleas at Manchester Magistrates’ Court on 11 November 2026, with the charges stemming from an alleged incident on Sawyer Street, Bury, on 6 August 2026.

Court records allege that Oldham had a machete in a public place without good reason or lawful authority. He is also accused of causing £300 worth of damage to windows belonging to a woman involved in the incident.

No finding of guilt has been made at this stage.

Oldham was granted conditional bail, which includes restrictions on entering Sawyer Street and contacting the woman, either directly or indirectly. The case is set to proceed to trial at Stockport Magistrates’ Court, with the trial scheduled for 2 August 2027, expected to last three hours.

The outcome of the trial will be closely monitored by local residents and authorities.

It has also been recognised as a finalist in the New Business of the Year category at the Rochdale Business Awards for two consecutive years.

The studio offers pottery painting sessions and workshops for schools and community organisations, and has collaborated with local entities such as Rochdale and District Mind.

Clay & Glaze has also participated in events like Rochdale Council's Ignite Fire Festival, further establishing its presence in the community.

The growth of Clay & Glaze reflects a broader trend of independent businesses thriving in Rochdale, contributing to the local economy and providing creative outlets for residents.

articles.title: Rochdale Council unveils £5.6m plan to improve temporary accommodation for homeless families
articles.excerpt: The council's new framework aims to enhance the quality and cost-effectiveness of temporary housing for vulnerable families in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has announced a £5.6 million plan to improve temporary accommodation for homeless families, addressing the needs of 387 households currently relying on such housing.

As of early November, 250 of these households include families with children, with some placed in hotels and B&Bs, which are costly and often substandard.

The new framework aims to provide better oversight and control over the types of housing offered to those at risk of homelessness.

The plan categorises accommodation into four 'Lots', with the first two lots focusing on B&Bs and nightly paid accommodation, estimated to cost £4.9 million. The council aims to reduce reliance on B&Bs while ensuring emergency options remain available when necessary.

The framework will allow housing providers to register with the council, ensuring they meet required standards before being accepted as trusted services.

Rochdale Council's cabinet is set to discuss and approve the plans next week, which are designed to create a more sustainable and effective approach to supporting vulnerable families in the borough.

  • The new framework aims to improve the quality of temporary accommodation for 387 households currently in need.

articles.content_html:
Greater Manchester Police (GMP) has applied for exceptional financial support from the government to address increasing pressures on its resources. This request comes as GMP faces challenges related to the growth of Greater Manchester, which has led to heightened demands on policing services.

Bev Craig, the Mayor of Greater Manchester, plans to meet with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood to discuss the funding issues facing GMP. Craig has reached out to the Home Office regarding the financial challenges and the need for additional support to maintain service levels.

Sir Stephen Watson, Chief Constable of GMP, stated that the force is well led and performing effectively despite the pressures.

Craig highlighted that the current national funding formula for police forces is considered unsustainable by local officials, indicating a need for reform to ensure adequate funding for GMP.

GMP is recognized as one of the best performing forces in the country, and local officials are advocating for a funding model that reflects the realities of policing in Greater Manchester.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Greater Manchester Police applies for exceptional financial support - Manchester Evening News ‌ ‌ Skip to main content Manchester Evening News: Number one for news, opinion, sport & celebrity news Greater Manchester Police applies for exceptional financial support The force has asked for more support amid growing concerns around its finances Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:51, 17 Nov 2026 Updated 10:01, 18 Nov 2026 GMP headquarters (Image: Kenny Brown / MEN) Greater Manchester Police (GMP) has applied for ‘exceptional financial support’ from the government amid major funding problems. ‌ ‌ Kate Green, Greater Manchester's deputy mayor, said on Monday (November 16) that GMP’s application for support has not yet got an outcome, and that Bev Craig is planning to meet with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood in the next few weeks. ‌ A report in September revealed GMP was facing a budget overspend predicted to hit nearly £10m this year. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter A document published by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) this week stated: ‘In 2026/27 GMP received an increase in Police Grant funding of 2.6 per cent, the second lowest increase nationally and compared to a national average increase of 3.2pc and increases of 4pc in London, 4.2pc in Kent and 3.6pc in Merseyside.’ Sir Stephen Watson, Chief Constable of Greater Manchester Police , said: “GMP is well led, well managed and full of determined public servants. Whilst there are many areas in which we seek to continue to improve, the force is currently performing well and is in a strong position. ‌ “What is important however, is that GMP's long-term success is not impacted by a failure to recognise that the structured funding requirement of the force is increasing in line with the growth and prominence of Greater Manchester. “This is not to suggest that GMP's performance is in any danger of declining in the short term. Our request for a review of the wider funding settlement merely recognises the growing pressures of the coming years.” ‌ GMP's Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson (Image: Ryan Jenkinson / Manchester Evening News) Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig said: "It's widely recognised that GMP are facing exceptional pressures as Greater Manchester grows. Last year we raised real concerns with ministers over the police funding settlement, which was one of the weakest in the country, and the pressure on GMP has only grown since then. ‌ "With extra policing and security required for No 10 North, increasing pressure from national protests and more high-level events coming to the city-region, the clear imbalance in national funding for police forces is now unsustainable. "Since coming into office in August, I have been in contact with Home Office and have been clear that this issue cannot wait any longer. GMP are now one of the best performing forces in the country and crime is going down. At a time when we must do all we can to make our communities feel safer, we need the national funding formula to reflect the work they actually do.” ‌ At Greater Manchester’s police, fire and crime panel on Monday, Stockport Councillor Dan Oliver asked whether GMP’s financial challenges could affect the police precept - the charge paid by Greater Manchester residents through their council tax bills to fund local policing. The police precept for 2027/28 will be set early next year. ‌ Councillor Oliver said: “It was referred to last time by the deputy mayor that GMP were applying for exceptional financial support to government, given that may have an impact on this [precept] process, do we have an outcome or indication of where that’s up to at a government level?” Responding, deputy mayor Kate Green said: “Colleagues will recall my reporting that the mayor was very reluctant to ask residents of Greater Manchester to bear more than their fair share of the cost of policing to keep our residents safe. ‌ “An initial meeting has taken place now with CIPFA [(the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy] who are commissioned by national government to look at our financial situation, our governance, our value for money and the approach with which we manage our resources. “We expect there will be further discussion as a result of that, we haven’t got an outcome to our application yet, the mayor expects to meet the home secretary in the next couple of weeks and we will be putting this issue on the agenda. ‌ “It remains our firm view that the issue GMP faces in relation to its funding is not poor financial management it is a funding formula that disadvantages metropolitan police forces, and I know the mayor is keen to make that point forcefully to the home secretary, as she has already in writing, to do so again when she meets her.” Deputy mayor Kate Green (Image: Anthony Moss / MEN) ‌ September’s report on GMP’s finances revealed the force is taking steps to try and balance the books including making savings and introducing ‘workforce controls’. Kate Green added in September that Andy Burnham opening Number 10 North in Manchester has piled ‘significant additional demands’ on Greater Manchester Police among other pressures on the force. ‌ A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said: “Greater Manchester Police is in the unique position of policing what is in effect, the second capital city of the country, with the resulting demand some other forces outside of London do not experience. “This is further exacerbated by, in our opinion, an outdated funding formula, which leads to an over reliance on the council taxbase of Greater Manchester, which has previously allowed us to create a 3.9 per cent increase in funding. This is below the national average of 4.5 per cent and led GMP to receive the second lowest funding settlement in England and Wales. ‌ “Despite this, GMP remains one of the best performing forces in the country, so we are confident this has not impacted on an operational level. Officers and staff continue to deliver the best possible performance they can, in spite of the extra pressures placed on them, as the force deals with increased demand due to the levels of regional and national focus it receives, without any additional government funding. “The force can demonstrate strong financial management over the past five years, and has a strong plan for the future, but the force remains in a uniquely challenging operating environment and as such a request has been made to the government for financial support which recognises this.” ‌ A Home Office spokesperson said: “Since the election, we have increased funding to policing by £2 billion. Police force funding this year is at a historic high of £18.5 billion. “We have established the Financial Resilience Framework to ensure a consistent approach to assessing financial resilience in policing. Article continues below “We are also reviewing the police funding formula to ensure the system is fair and continues to prioritise public safety. articles.title: LIVE: No injuries reported after suspected gas explosion at Bamford house as emergency services remain
articles.excerpt: Police and the fire service say no injuries have been reported after a suspected gas explosion at a house in Bamford at around 4.30pm. Bury Road is closed from Midgehall Drive to Woodtop Avenue.
articles.content_html:
No injuries have been reported after a suspected gas explosion at a house in Bamford on Tuesday 17 November, police and the fire service have said.

Greater Manchester Police said it received reports of a suspected explosion at an address on Camberley Drive at around 4.30pm. Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service described the house as being on Bury Road, and said crews were called shortly after 4.30pm.

Police, fire and ambulance crews remain at the scene. Bury Road is closed from Midgehall Drive to Woodtop Avenue, and debris was left across the road.

Three fire engines from Heywood and Rochdale fire stations and the Special Response Vehicle from Ashton-under-Lyne were sent. Firefighters are working with Cadent Gas, Greater Manchester Police and North West Ambulance Service to make the area safe.

A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said: “Shortly after 4.30pm on Tuesday 17 November, three fire engines from Heywood and Rochdale fire stations, and the Special Response Vehicle from Ashton-under-Lyne fire station, were called to reports of a gas explosion at a house on Bury Road, Rochdale.

“Crews arrived quickly and are working alongside Cadent Gas, Greater Manchester Police and North West Ambulance to make the area safe.

“Firefighters remain in attendance at this time.”

A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police said: “We received reports of a suspected explosion at an address on Camberley Drive, Rochdale at around 4.30pm.

“Emergency services are in attendance. No injuries have been reported and enquiries are ongoing.”

Witness Carol Scott said: “Just been an explosion at a house on Bury Road, Bamford, suspected gas explosion. Debris all over Bury Road which is cordoned off. Police and the fire service are at the scene now. Our house shook violently, I thought a plane had landed on us, it was very scary.”

Ms Scott later said a neighbour had checked on the owner of the house. She said: “A neighbour went to see the owner and he was uninjured luckily but I think they took him to hosp for a check.”

Rochdale Daily has asked Bamford ward councillors Angela Smith, Stephen Anstee and Phil Beal, and Norden ward councillor Paul Ellison MBE, for comment.

This story will be updated as more information becomes available.

Source: Greater Manchester Police and Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service statements; witness Carol Scott; Rochdale Daily newsdesk, 17 November 2026.

articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has awarded a £4.8 million contract for the Rochdale Borough Specialist Health Improvement Service to The Big Life Company Limited. The contract will run from 2027 to 2030.

This procurement was conducted under the Competitive Process of The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, ensuring a structured selection process for health service providers.

The Big Life Company Limited will deliver health improvement services aimed at enhancing the well-being of residents in the borough, reflecting the council's commitment to improving public health outcomes in Rochdale.

This contract is part of a broader strategy to address health inequalities and promote healthier lifestyles among the community.

articles.title: Former Clean Air Zone cameras now used by police to fight crime across Greater Manchester
articles.excerpt: Around 400 number plate cameras put up for the scrapped Clean Air Zone have been handed to Greater Manchester Police, with a senior officer saying they have led to multiple arrests.
articles.content_html:
Around 400 number plate cameras installed for Greater Manchester's scrapped Clean Air Zone, which would have covered Rochdale borough roads, are now being used by police to fight crime.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) has taken ownership of the automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras and linked them into its existing ANPR network, according to a Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) report.

Until now, officers could use footage and number plate data from the cameras only after asking permission from Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM), which owned them. The combined authority said that process delayed investigations.

Speaking at Greater Manchester's police, fire and crime panel on Monday 16 November, deputy mayor Kate Green said: "They are not speed cameras, they are being used for crime detection and as an investigative tool."

Deputy Chief Constable Terry Woods told the panel: "I cannot say strongly enough just what a difference that is making."

"It's been tangible, multiple arrests on the back of that system and it's keeping people safe," Mr Woods said, according to the Manchester Evening News.

The cameras were put up across the city region ahead of a charging Clean Air Zone, under which drivers of the most polluting vehicles would have paid up to £60 a day.

The charging scheme was shelved after a backlash. In January 2025 the Government approved Greater Manchester's investment-led Clean Air Plan, which has no charges to drive on local roads.

A six-week public consultation on handing the cameras to police ran from 23 September to 6 November 2025 and drew 4,830 responses.

Of those, 89.7 per cent agreed the cameras' main use should switch to crime detection, while 7.1 per cent disagreed. Rochdale borough residents made up 9.4 per cent of respondents.

Privacy was the most common concern, raised by 38.2 per cent of respondents, followed by data sharing at 37 per cent.

A report to the GM Air Quality Administration Committee in January said 372 Clean Air-funded cameras were operational. The committee decided on 29 January 2026 that GMP would take them over.

GMP is paying the transfer and running costs, according to Clean Air Greater Manchester. TfGM will still receive camera data to monitor the Clean Air Plan, but will not have access to live data.

Greater Manchester remains under a government direction to bring nitrogen dioxide levels on local roads within legal limits in the shortest possible time and by 2026.

Source: Greater Manchester Combined Authority committee report (29 January 2026), Clean Air Greater Manchester, and Manchester Evening News reporting of the Greater Manchester police, fire and crime panel. Photograph: Rochdale Daily image library.

articles.title: Rochdale teenagers born in 2009 or later will never be legally sold tobacco from 1 January
articles.excerpt: The generational smoking ban starts on 1 January 2027, making it an offence to sell tobacco to anyone born on or after 1 January 2009.
articles.content_html:
Young people in Rochdale borough born on or after 1 January 2009 will never be legally sold tobacco once the generational smoking ban takes effect on 1 January 2027.

The Department of Health and Social Care began a countdown to the change on Monday 16 November, with a campaign run jointly with the NHS.

From 1 January 2027 it becomes an offence to sell tobacco, herbal smoking products or cigarette papers to anyone born on or after 1 January 2009, under the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026.

The cut-off does not move. In practice, the legal age for buying tobacco rises by one year every year, so the first group affected, who turn 18 during 2027, will never be able to buy it.

Anyone born before 1 January 2009 can still be sold tobacco as now.

The department described the law as "a once-in-a-generation opportunity to protect future generations from tobacco addiction".

When the bill became law in April, Health Secretary Wes Streeting said: "This legislation marks a turning point for the nation's health."

Shops selling tobacco will have to check whether customers were born on or after 1 January 2009.

They must also display a new notice stating: "It is illegal to sell tobacco products to anyone born on or after 1 January 2009."

The Act received Royal Assent on 29 April 2026. It also bans advertising and sponsorship of vapes and nicotine products, and gives ministers powers to restrict packaging and displays that appeal to children.

A retail licensing scheme and stronger action against illicit tobacco and vapes are also part of the law, according to the government.

Smoking causes about 80,000 deaths a year in the UK and is the leading preventable cause of death, the government says. There are an estimated 5.3 million smokers in the UK.

Rochdale has a higher smoking rate than England as a whole. Rochdale Borough Council's needs assessment puts it at 15.3 per cent of adults in 2021, against 12.7 per cent nationally.

A YouGov survey in August 2024 found 61 per cent of UK adults supported the ban for those born on or after 1 January 2009, with 27 per cent against.

The ban comes into force on Friday 1 January 2027.

Source: Department of Health and Social Care Facebook post, 16 November 2026; GOV.UK; Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026; Rochdale Borough Council Joint Strategic Needs Assessment. Photograph: UK Government / NHS.

Corrections or right of reply: news@rochdaledaily.co.uk.

What changes in Rochdale

  • From 1 January 2027 it becomes an offence to sell tobacco, herbal smoking products or cigarette papers to anyone born on or after 1 January 2009.
  • Anyone born before 1 January 2009 can still be sold tobacco as now.
  • Shops selling tobacco will have to check whether customers were born on or after 1 January 2009.

articles.title: Hiram Boateng charged with affray after pitch invasion incident during York City-Rochdale match
articles.excerpt: Former MK Dons midfielder Hiram Boateng faces charges following an altercation with a fan during a pitch invasion at a match against Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
Hiram Boateng, 30, a midfielder for York City, has been charged with affray following an incident during a match against Rochdale in April 2026.

The altercation occurred after a pitch invasion during the game, which ended in a 1-1 draw and saw York City promoted from the National League at Rochdale's expense.

The incident involved two pitch invasions: the first occurred when Rochdale scored in the 95th minute, leading their fans to believe they had won the title. However, York City equalised shortly after, prompting a second invasion at full-time.

It is during this second invasion that Boateng is alleged to have struck a Rochdale fan.

Boateng appeared in magistrates' court in Manchester, where no pleas were entered. He is accused of using threatening, abusive or insulting behaviour with intent to cause fear of or provoke violence.

A statement from York City confirmed they are working with authorities to understand the circumstances surrounding the incident, and that Boateng has the club's full support.

York City co-owner Matt Uggla defended Boateng on social media, questioning the accountability of the fan who invaded the pitch and provoked the situation. He expressed frustration that Boateng is facing a criminal charge while the fan remains unaccountable.

articles.title: Heywood homes left without power after cable fault during snow warning
articles.excerpt: Sixty-five properties in north Heywood lost power on Tuesday morning, with engineers aiming to restore supplies by 12.30pm.
articles.content_html:
Sixty-five homes and businesses in north Heywood were left without power on Tuesday morning after an underground cable fault during a snow warning.

SP Electricity North West, which runs the local network, said the properties were hit by an unexpected incident with the underground cable that supplies them.

Engineers were on their way, with a target of restoring power by 12.30pm, according to the operator's incident log reported by the Rochdale Times.

The affected postcodes are OL10 1AA, OL10 1AB, OL10 1AL, OL10 1DT, OL10 1FH, OL10 1FJ, OL10 1FL and OL10 1FN.

Heywood was one of several places hit across Greater Manchester, with almost 500 properties without power at around 7am, according to the operator's figures.

The largest outages were in Saddleworth, where 191 properties were affected, Cadishead and Lower Irlam in Salford, with 126, and Ashton Hurst in Tameside, with 104.

The operator has put the faults down to underground cables and has not said the weather caused them.

It told customers it had no warning before the power went off, and said digging to repair underground cables can make a power cut last longer.

A Met Office yellow warning for snow covered Greater Manchester from midnight until 11am, with forecasters warning of a small chance of power cuts.

The UK Health Security Agency also has a yellow cold-health alert in place for the North West until 9am on Thursday 19 November.

Anyone without power can report it or get updates by calling 105 or 0800 195 4141, which are free from mobiles and landlines.

Residents who need extra help during a power cut, such as those relying on medical equipment, can join the operator's free Extra Care Register.
